spatialBenefitAssessment: Potential genuine benefit: a support repair occupies the same physical space a boat needs, so independently inspecting support and clearance can expose competing requirements beyond the recommended invoice video. The hidden split alone is not sufficient justification. Current runtime framing fails to expose the important counterfactual, and guided discovery is too linear.

findings.issue: The failed-repair capture does not visibly establish why the boat cannot pass.
findings.requestedChange: In startTest choose an oblique channel-wide test view showing the full hull, prop contact, pier and deck; retain that inspectable final pose. Move or shrink the foreground gauge so it cannot mask the contact. Do not rely on a caption announcing blockage.
findings.evidence: captures/missing-clearance.png crops the boat at the right edge and hides the prop/contact behind the close pier/gauge view; browser-initial.json reports the same defect. startTest never calls ctx.view.

findings.issue: The keyboard investigation cannot select the lane-only counterfactual or remove a finding; inspection automatically supplies it.
findings.requestedChange: Use the first action to cycle four explicit handoff states (request only, support, clearance, both), with the second running the repair. Keep free inspection and optional object picks synchronized with that state. Preserve two controls plus Reset; make camera inspection distinct from claiming a finding was supplied.
findings.evidence: inspectNext selects support before clearance, adds it immediately, and eventually disables itself. chooseRepair supports lane-only but the keyboard route cannot reach it; intent acknowledges this.

findings.issue: Deterministic repair captions overstate what missing or complete context causes.
findings.requestedChange: Describe these as authored example repairs and state that missing evidence can be rediscovered and complete context does not ensure compliance. Replace the lane-only assertion that the lane gives no reason to inspect underneath with a statement about this particular repair choice.
findings.evidence: CAPTION.patchLane says the lane constraint gives no reason to look under the deck; fallback says each handoff produces its outcome. The guide exercise explicitly says not to force failure if the agent independently discovers the rule.

findings.issue: Runtime contrast and incidental detail compete with the explanatory geometry.
findings.requestedChange: Reduce railing repetitions, keep structural outlines stronger than water/hidden edges, and make the split and underpin footprint identifiable without amber being their only cue. Frame the successful repair obliquely enough to show its support geometry alongside the open channel.
findings.evidence: initial.png has dense fine rail lines; under-span.png is dominated by the gauge; complete-handoff.png shows a clear lane but does not clearly expose the claimed underpin repair. Poster outlines are much stronger than browser outlines.

requiredVerification: Coordinator: capture all four handoffs at 420px and desktop, including patch settlement, full boat/prop contact, and underpin footprint with open lane.
Verify keyboard-only reaches every handoff and switching a handoff clears old results. Verify Reset, reduced motion and idle-on-load in the actual viewer.

Verify picks cannot select hidden crack through deck, pier or gauge; water and clearance overlay must not intercept intended picks. Confirm a learner can distinguish repair outcomes from geometry with captions temporarily hidden.

Review method: source/transcript reading and supplied image inspection only; no shared browser use, independent runtime test, video playback or implementation changes. Coordinator owns final verification.
